tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 growth drivers

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 growth drivers

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was a record **$51.2 billion in Q3 FY2026** (quarter ended October 26, 2025), increasing **25% sequentially** and **66% year over year**. [[1]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **GB300/Blackwell production ramp:** Data Center compute revenue increased **56% year over year**, driven principally by the ramp of GB300 systems; GB300 had overtaken GB200 and represented roughly **two-thirds of Blackwell revenue** during the quarter. [[2]] [[3]]
- **Sustained AI-infrastructure capacity demand:** NVIDIA said cloud GPUs were sold out and that its installed GPU base—including Blackwell, Hopper, and Ampere—was fully utilized, reflecting continuing demand for both AI model training and inference workloads. [[1]] [[2]]
- **Networking became a material incremental contributor:** Networking revenue reached **$8.2 billion**, up **162% year over year**, supported by NVLink scale-up and double-digit growth in Spectrum-X Ethernet and Quantum-X InfiniBand. [[4]]
- **System-scale AI-factory deployments:** Large customer projects supported demand for GPUs and networking together, including AWS and HUMAIN’s planned deployment of up to 150,000 AI accelerators and xAI/HUMAIN’s 500-megawatt data-center initiative. [[2]]
- **Broader adoption of NVIDIA switching in AI clusters:** NVIDIA stated that a majority of AI deployments included its switches, with Ethernet GPU attach rates roughly comparable with InfiniBand; Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, and xAI were cited as building gigawatt-scale AI factories using Spectrum-X Ethernet. [[2]] 

In short, the 66% Data Center growth was not solely a GPU-volume story: it combined the high-value GB300 transition, exceptional AI-compute demand, and rapidly expanding sales of NVIDIA’s interconnect and networking stack. [[3]] [[4]]
